## Catalysts

* Catalysts lower a reaction's activation energy, providing an alternate pathway for the reaction to take place. There are two types of catalysts: homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts.
* Homogeneous catalysts are catalysts that are in the same state as the reactants. These catalysts are used in the reaction and are regenerated by the end of the reaction.
* Heterogeneous catalysts are catalysts that are in a different state from the reactants. These work by adsorption, where molecules are adsorbed onto the active site on the catalyst surface so the reaction can occur. This allows closer proximity of the reactants and weakens the bonds in the reactants so the products can form more easily. The products are then desorbed from the catalyst.
